title: Wildlife & Animal Kingdom
description: 36 original questions on habitats, animal records, collective nouns, and wildlife silhouettes.
author: QuizRooms

questions.prompt: Which marine mammal illustrated here is the largest animal ever known to have lived on Earth?
questions.explanation: Blue whales can reach 30 meters in length and weigh up to 180 metric tons.

questions.prompt: Which long-necked savanna mammal illustrated here is the tallest living terrestrial animal?
questions.explanation: Adult giraffes stand up to 5.5 meters tall yet have the same 7 neck vertebrae as humans.

questions.prompt: Which flightless bird illustrated here is the tallest and heaviest of all living penguin species?
questions.explanation: Emperor penguins breed during the harsh Antarctic winter.

questions.prompt: Which largest living land animal illustrated here is recognizable by its huge ears shaped roughly like Africa?
questions.explanation: African bush elephants can weigh over 6,000 kg.

questions.prompt: What is the fastest land animal in the world?
questions.explanation: Cheetahs can accelerate from 0 to 100 km/h in about 3 seconds.

questions.prompt: What is the fastest bird in the world during a hunting dive?
questions.explanation: Peregrine falcons exceed 320 km/h (200 mph) in a high-speed stoop.

questions.prompt: What is a group of lions called?
questions.explanation: A pride typically consists of related females, their cubs, and a small coalition of males.

questions.prompt: What is a group of crows famously called?
questions.explanation: A group of owls is a 'parliament', while a group of crows is a 'murder'.

questions.prompt: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.explanation: Two branchial hearts pump blood to the gills and one systemic heart pumps it to the body.

questions.prompt: Which mammal is the only mammal capable of true sustained flight?
questions.explanation: Bats make up about 20% of all classified mammal species.

questions.prompt: Which two mammals are the only monotremes (egg-laying mammals) alive today?
questions.explanation: Both are native to Australia and New Guinea.

questions.prompt: Which Australian marsupial sleeps up to 18–20 hours a day and feeds almost exclusively on eucalyptus leaves?
questions.explanation: Eucalyptus leaves are low in energy and toxic to most other mammals.

questions.prompt: Which bird can fly backward as well as hover effortlessly in midair?
questions.explanation: Hummingbirds beat their wings in a figure-eight pattern up to 80 times per second.

questions.prompt: What is the largest living species of lizard?
questions.explanation: Found on Indonesian islands, Komodo dragons can grow up to 3 meters long.

questions.prompt: Which whale is the deepest-diving mammal on Earth, hunting giant squid over 2,000 meters down?
questions.explanation: Cuvier's beaked whale and sperm whales are among Earth's deepest-diving mammals.

questions.prompt: Which animal has the longest gestation period of any land mammal (about 22 months)?
questions.explanation: Elephants carry their calves for nearly two full years.

questions.prompt: Which Arctic marine mammal is famous for its long spiral tusk (actually an elongated tooth)?
questions.explanation: The narwhal's tusk can grow up to 3 meters long and is packed with sensory nerve endings.

questions.prompt: Which big cat is the largest feline species in the world?
questions.explanation: Siberian and Bengal tigers can exceed 300 kg.

questions.prompt: Which African animal is responsible for more human fatalities in Africa than lions or crocodiles?
questions.explanation: Despite being herbivores, hippos are fiercely territorial in rivers and lakes.

questions.prompt: What is the only continent on Earth with NO native land snakes?
questions.explanation: Iceland, Ireland, and New Zealand are also snake-free islands, and Antarctica is the only snake-free continent.

questions.prompt: Which marine animal is actually the largest member of the dolphin family?
questions.explanation: Orcas (killer whales) are apex oceanic predators belonging to Delphinidae.

questions.prompt: Which shark is the largest living fish species on Earth (and a gentle filter feeder)?
questions.explanation: Whale sharks can exceed 12 meters in length and feed mainly on plankton.

questions.prompt: Which African bird is the largest and heaviest living bird on Earth?
questions.explanation: Ostriches cannot fly but can sprint at up to 70 km/h.

questions.prompt: Which mammal is the most heavily trafficked wild mammal in the world, covered in keratin scales?
questions.explanation: Pangolins curl into an armored ball when threatened.

questions.prompt: Which shark species is known to live longer than any other vertebrate — estimated over 250–400 years?
questions.explanation: Living in frigid Arctic waters gives the Greenland shark an ultra-slow metabolism.

questions.prompt: What is the collective noun for a group of owls?
questions.explanation: Made famous by C.S. Lewis, a group of owls is called a parliament.

questions.prompt: Which tiny, brightly colored frog family in Central and South America is among the most toxic animals on Earth?
questions.explanation: Their skin toxins come from the ants and beetles they eat in the wild.

questions.prompt: Which animal has cube-shaped droppings that prevent them from rolling off rocks?
questions.explanation: Wombats use their cubic droppings to mark territory.

questions.prompt: What is the largest living rodent in the world, native to South America?
questions.explanation: Capybaras are semi-aquatic herbivores that can weigh over 60 kg.

questions.prompt: Which migratory butterfly travels thousands of kilometers from Canada to central Mexico each autumn?
questions.explanation: The round-trip migration takes multiple generations to complete.

questions.prompt: Which ocean creature is nicknamed the 'immortal jellyfish' because it can revert to its juvenile polyp stage?
questions.explanation: Under stress, Turritopsis dohrnii can reset its cellular life cycle.

questions.prompt: Which primate is humanity's closest living genetic relative alongside the bonobo?
questions.explanation: Humans share roughly 98.7% of their DNA sequence with chimpanzees and bonobos.

questions.prompt: Which seabird has the largest wingspan of any living bird (up to 3.5 meters)?
questions.explanation: Albatrosses can glide for hours over the Southern Ocean without flapping their wings.

questions.prompt: Which creature's blood is copper-based (hemocyanin), making it appear blue?
questions.explanation: Horseshoe crab blood is also widely used in medical safety testing.

questions.prompt: Which marsupial is the only marsupial native to North America?
questions.explanation: Opossums are famous for 'playing possum' when threatened.

questions.prompt: Which big cat is the only one that cannot roar (it purrs instead)?
questions.explanation: Lions, tigers, jaguars, and leopards have a specialized hyoid bone that lets them roar; cheetahs do not.
